issue.title: test: Library subprocess fixtures fail the temporary HOME check on Linux
issue.body:
A full `go test -tags nogui ./... -timeout=45m` run on Linux/amd64 with Go 1.26.8 fails in `internal/library`: several subprocess tests are rejected by `testenv` because their fixture HOME is a sibling of the package's private temporary directory.

I reproduced a representative failure on **unmodified main, 3d0d790**, independently of a Responses WebSocket change:

```sh
(
  set -o pipefail
  umask 022
  verification_home=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'chmod -R u+w "$verification_home"; rm -rf "$verification_home"' EXIT
  verification_gopath=$(go env GOPATH)
  verification_modcache=$(go env GOMODCACHE)
  verification_buildcache=$(go env GOCACHE)
  HOME="$verification_home" TMPDIR="$verification_home" GOTMPDIR="$verification_home" \
    GOPATH="$verification_gopath" GOMODCACHE="$verification_modcache" GOCACHE="$verification_buildcache" \
    go test -tags nogui ./internal/library \
      -run '^TestCheckStdio$/^starts_in_the_home_directory$' -count=1 -timeout=1m
)
```

Result (temporary directory suffixes shortened):

```text
--- FAIL: TestCheckStdio
    --- FAIL: TestCheckStdio/starts_in_the_home_directory
        mcp_check_test.go:188: got {State:error ...
        Detail:testenv: HOME is "/tmp/verification/TestCheckStdiostarts_in_the_home_directory.../002",
        outside the temporary folder /tmp/verification/magpie-library-test-...
        ...}, want ok
FAIL github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/library
```

`internal/library/main_test.go` creates `magpie-library-test-*` and sets `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, and `TEMP` to it before `testenv.Run`. The child sees that directory as `os.TempDir()`, while the fixture HOME above was created outside it; `testenv.checkChild` then rejects the child. Expected: the fixture subprocess starts inside the test sandbox and the stdio check succeeds.

The full run also reports this rejection in `TestEnvRefsFromLoginShell/command`, other `TestCheckStdio` subtests, `TestCheckServersOnce`, and several MCP hub/WSL checks. This report groups the shared isolation failure rather than opening one issue per test. The test sandbox check should remain intact.

I checked #2765 and #1727: those concern a startup timeout and the real server's working directory respectively, whereas this reproduction fails immediately at the test isolation check. No fix for this separate test issue is included in the WebSocket change.

comments.body:
Fixed on [fix/5290-library-fixture-gotmpdir](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5290-library-fixture-gotmpdir), commit [c76d6b39](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/c76d6b39fc1ce70b09ef4bcb5e6fbf589fffdf2d), based on upstream `ed0ab567`.

The missing variable is `GOTMPDIR`: Go's `testing.T.TempDir` prefers it over the OS temporary directory. The Library test entry point now sets it to the same private temporary root as `TMPDIR`, `TMP` and `TEMP`. `testenv.checkChild` remains unchanged.

With an outer `GOTMPDIR`, the original `TestCheckStdio/starts_in_the_home_directory` fails immediately because its fixture HOME is outside the package root; the patch passes that reproduction. Related stdio, login-shell, server and selected hub/WSL fixtures pass, including scoped race tests and package vet. A real child given an escaped HOME still fails the sandbox check. I independently reran the original failing subprocess test.

Validated on Linux with Go 1.27.3. No full suite/build or Go 1.26.8/macOS/Windows/real-WSL run was performed. AI-assisted implementation and review.

issue.title: [Patch] Responses WebSocket clients omitting the HTTP stream field receive buffered replies

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
A tested fix is available below. I attempted to open a PR, but GitHub rejected `CreatePullRequest` for this account. Following the [contributor guide](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/docs/contributors.md), which says PRs are open to collaborators only and reporter fixes can arrive in issues, I am submitting the patch here.

- **Commit:** [62e3fd1ad36eeec25fc628d21db79c467f490c07](https://github.com/AnacondaKC/magpie/commit/62e3fd1ad36eeec25fc628d21db79c467f490c07)
- **Branch:** [AnacondaKC/magpie:fix/responses-ws-stream](https://github.com/AnacondaKC/magpie/tree/fix/responses-ws-stream)
- **Diff:** https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...AnacondaKC:magpie:fix/responses-ws-stream
- **Patch:** https://github.com/AnacondaKC/magpie/commit/62e3fd1ad36eeec25fc628d21db79c467f490c07.patch

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/AnacondaKC/magpie.git fix/responses-ws-stream
git cherry-pick 62e3fd1ad36eeec25fc628d21db79c467f490c07
```

The patch changes one production behavior, adds one end-to-end regression, and updates the owning reference (3 files, 62 insertions, 1 deletion). It was prepared against main at `3d0d790` after observing the problem with magpie `0.1.2994`.

Standard Responses WebSocket clients omit `stream`, as documented by OpenAI. Magpie currently carries that omission into its internal HTTP request, which can select the non-streaming path. The client then receives a completed response converted into WebSocket frames, without the incremental text events needed for live output and time-to-first-token measurement.

### Official protocol behavior

OpenAI's [WebSocket mode guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/websocket-mode#connect-and-create-responses) explicitly states:

> The payload mirrors the normal Responses create body, except that transport-specific fields like `stream` and `background` are not used.

Its official `response.create` examples omit `stream` and consume `response.output_text.delta` events. Omitting `stream: true` is therefore the documented WebSocket behavior, rather than a missing client setting. Clients should not need to add an HTTP-specific field to obtain streamed WebSocket responses.

### Change

Set `stream: true` when converting a generating WebSocket turn into the internal HTTP request. This preserves streaming semantics across `/v1/responses`, `/responses`, and the Codex backend Responses socket, which share this conversion point. `generate: false` warmups still return locally before the conversion, and ordinary HTTP POST requests keep their existing behavior.

Update the gateway routing reference to describe the distinction between the external WebSocket request and the internal HTTP request.

### Regression test

`TestResponsesSocketStreamsWithoutStreamField` sends a `response.create` frame without `stream` through the gateway's real `Front` stack to a local fake Responses provider. The provider sends and flushes a text delta, then waits on a channel before completing. The client must receive that delta before releasing the provider; the test then checks the completed text and usage. This verifies actual incremental delivery without timing sleeps or external model requests.

On unmodified `main` (`3d0d790`), the new test fails with:

```text
no text delta before the upstream completed
```

The received frames are `response.created`, `response.output_item.done`, and `response.completed`, with no text delta. The test passes with the fix.

### Validation

Go 1.26.8, Linux/amd64. Tests use a temporary HOME with pinned Go caches; the full suite uses umask 022 and matching TMPDIR/GOTMPDIR.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regression against unmodified production code | Fails with the missing-delta message above |
| WS regression set (`TestResponsesSocket`, `TestCodexSocket`, `TestHeldTurn`, `TestSocketTurn`) | Pass |
| Same WS regression set with `-race` | Pass |
| Full `internal/gateway` package, as part of the full suite | Pass (468.653s) |
| `gofmt -l` on the changed Go files; `git diff --check` | Clean |
| `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` | Pass |
| `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` | Pass |
| `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui` | Pass |
| `GOOS=windows go build` | Pass |
| `go vet ./...`; `go build` with the Linux desktop GUI | Blocked by missing gtk4, webkitgtk-6.0, and libsoup-3.0 development libraries |
| `go test -tags nogui ./... -timeout=45m` | Fails in `internal/library`; see #5290 |

For #5290, `TestCheckStdio/starts_in_the_home_directory` was also run on **unmodified main at 3d0d790** and fails with the same temporary HOME rejection. This separate test issue is reported rather than hidden or changed as part of the WS fix. No full-suite pass is claimed.

Not run: live provider/Niko integration, desktop runtime or GUI browser tests. The regression uses local HTTP/WebSocket servers and does not consume model quota.
